Using Supplementary Table S1D at the exact amino-acid change level (gene + AAmut), no specific mutation was significantly enriched in responders or non-responders after multiple-testing correction.
I tested 304 recurrent specific mutations (observed in at least 2 patients) across 21 responders and 17 non-responders with two-sided Fisher exact tests and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction; the smallest raw p-value was for PCDHB8 S177F in non-responders (0/21 responders vs 3/17 non-responders, p=0.0806, q=0.9068), which was not significant after FDR correction.
Other recurrent exact mutations also failed significance after correction, including BRAF V600E (6/21 vs 7/17), BRAF V600K (2/21 vs 2/17), NRAS Q61K (3/21 vs 0/17), and OR13C5 M185I (3/21 vs 0/17).
For context, the provided gene-level summary sheet S1E reported several genes enriched at the gene level rather than the exact-mutation level. Significant responder-enriched genes in S1E were FREM1, OR13C5, FMO1, UTRN, LPHN3, MUC12, ZNF534, SP140L, ITGA9, AMER3, ABCA7, OR10J1, and BRCA2 (BH-adjusted pAdjR < 0.05). Significant non-responder-enriched genes in S1E were TRPM2 and CLEC14A (BH-adjusted pAdjNR < 0.05).
Therefore, the strict answer to the question about specific mutations is: none reached statistical significance after correcting for multiple testing in this cohort.
